claims.text: Machine-learning optimization of processing parameters can produce a microstructure that simultaneously enhances strength and ductility through multiple deformation mechanisms.
Conventional strengthening methods such as grain refinement, precipitation hardening, and cold working typically increase strength at the expense of ductility.
Machine-learning algorithms can analyze large experimental and simulation datasets for processing optimization.
Machine learning can identify non-intuitive combinations of temperature, strain rate, and alloying additions.
The processing conditions identified by machine learning can produce optimized microstructures.
High strength and ductility are both important under ambient or standard mechanical-testing conditions.
Beneficial distributions of phases, nanoprecipitates, coherent interfaces, or related structures can contribute to simultaneous strength and ductility improvement.
Lamellar structures are an example of a microstructural feature that produces the proposed strength–ductility improvement.
The optimized microstructure promotes simultaneous activation of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity.
A machine-learning framework can correlate processing parameters with microstructural outcomes.
Machine learning can pinpoint conditions under which multiple plasticity mechanisms are activated concurrently.
Concurrent deformation mechanisms reduce localized stress concentrations and delay crack initiation.
The proposed microstructural mechanism can retain high yield strength while improving ductility.
Materials processed under machine-learning-optimized conditions will have a significantly better strength–ductility balance than conventionally processed materials.
The success of machine-learning processing optimization depends on comprehensive, high-quality datasets.
The approach may be ineffective when alloy-system data are insufficient or relevant processing phenomena are poorly represented.
The magnitude of any strength and ductility improvement is uncertain until experimentally validated.
Machine-learning-predicted processing conditions may require further refinement.
